# Process Design Document (synthetic): student club

> Synthetic document generated for the Goal 1 experiment from the BIRD mini-dev descriptions. It stands in for a Cartographer PDD: business language, no system identifiers.

## 1. Purpose

The team responsible for student club wants its day-to-day questions answered without hand-written queries. This document records what the team works with, in their words, and the questions they ask.

## 2. What the team keeps track of

### Event

For each event the team records: a unique identifier for the event; event name; the date the event took place or is scheduled to take place; the kind of event, such as game, social, election; a free text field for any notes about the event; address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location; one of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed.
- event date: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00
- status: Open/ Closed/ Planning

### Major

For each major the team records: a unique identifier for each major; major name; the name of the department that offers the major; the name college that houses the department that offers the major.

### Zip code

For each zip code the team records: the ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office; the kind of ZIP code; the city to which the ZIP pertains; the county to which the ZIP pertains; the name of the state to which the ZIP pertains; the abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains.

### Attendance

For each attendance the team records: the unique identifier of the event which was attended; the unique identifier of the member who attended the event.
- link to event: References the Event table
- link to member: References the Member table

### Budget

For each budget the team records: a unique identifier for the budget entry; the area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking; the total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event; a value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; the amount budgeted for the specified category and event; the status of the event; the unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.
- spent: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining: the unit is dollar
- amount: the unit is dollar
- event status: Closed / Open/ Planning
- link to event: References the Event table

### Expense

For each expense the team records: unique id of income; a textual description of what the money was spend for; the date the expense was incurred; the dollar amount of the expense; a true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; the member who incurred the expense; the unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.
- expense date: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost: the unit is dollar
- approved: true/ false
- link to budget: References the Budget table

### Income

For each income the team records: a unique identifier for each record of income; the date that the fund received; amount of funds; a value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation; a free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds; link to member.
- amount: the unit is dollar

### Member

For each member the team records: unique id of member; member's first name; member's last name; member's email; the position the member holds in the club; the size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; the best telephone at which to contact the member; the zip code of the member's hometown; the unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table.

## 3. Questions the team asks

- What's Angela Sanders's major? (they explain: Angela Sanders is the full name; full name refers to first_name, last_name; major refers to major_name)
- Among the students from the Student_Club who attended the event "Women's Soccer", how many of them want a T-shirt that's in medium size? (they explain: Women's Soccer is an event name; T-shirt that is in medium size refers to t_shirt_size = 'Medium')
- Among the events attended by more than 10 members of the Student_Club, how many of them are meetings? (they explain: meetings events refers to type = 'Meeting'; attended by more than 10 members refers to COUNT(event_id) > 10)
- List all the names of events that had an attendance of over 20 students but were not fundraisers. (they explain: name of events refers to event_name; attendance of over 20 students COUNT(event_id) > 20)
- What is the amount of the funds that the Vice President received? (they explain: 'Vice President' is a position of Student Club; funds received refers to amount)
- List the full name of the Student_Club members that grew up in Illinois state. (they explain: full name of member refers to first_name, last_name)
- Was each expense in October Meeting on October 8, 2019 approved? (they explain: event_name = 'October Meeting' where event_date = '2019-10-08'; approved = True means expenses was approved; approved = False means expenses was not approved)
- Calculate the total average cost that Elijah Allen spent in the events on September and October. (they explain: Elijah Allen is the full name; full name refers to first_name, last_name; The 5th and 6th string of the expense_date in the expense table can refer to month; events in September and October refers to month(expense_date) = 9 OR month(expense_date) = 10)
- Calculate the difference of the total amount spent in all events by the Student_Club in year 2019 and 2020. (they explain: The first 4 strings of the event_date values in the event table can represent year; The difference of the total amount spent = SUBTRACT(spent where YEAR(event_date) = 2019, spent where YEAR(event_date) = 2020))
- What was the notes of the fundraising on 2019/9/14? (they explain: fundraising on 2019/9/14 refers to source = 'Fundraising' where date_received = '2019-09-14')
- Tell the phone number of "Carlo Jacobs". (they explain: Carlo Jacobs is the full name; full name refers to first_name, last_name)
- What is the status of the event which bought "Post Cards, Posters" on 2019/8/20? (they explain: 'Post Cards, Posters' is an expense description; on 2019/8/20 refers to expense_date = '2019-8-20'; status of event refers to event_status)
- What was Brent Thomason's major? (they explain: Brent Thomason is the full name; full name refers to first_name, last_name; major refers to major_name)
- For all the club members from "Business" major, how many of them wear medium size t-shirt? (they explain: 'Business' is a major name; wear medium size t-shirt refers to t_shirt_size = 'Medium')
- Which department was the President of the club in? (they explain: 'President' is a position of Student Club)
- State the date Connor Hilton paid his/her dues. (they explain: Connor Hilton is the full name; full name refers to first_name, last_name; date the dues was paid refers to date_received where source = 'Dues')
- How many times was the budget in Advertisement for "Yearly Kickoff" meeting more than "October Meeting"? (they explain: budget in Advertisement refer to category = 'Advertisement' in the budget table; DIVIDE(SUM(amount when event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff'), SUM(amount when event_name = 'October Meeting')))
- What is the total cost of the pizzas for all the events? (they explain: total cost of the pizzas refers to SUM(cost) where expense_description = 'Pizza')
- How many cities are there in Orange County, Virginia? (they explain: Orange County is the county name, Virginia is the state name)
- What does the person with the phone number "809-555-3360" major in? (they explain: major in refers to major_name)
- How many members attended the "Women's Soccer" event? (they explain: 'Women's Soccer' is the event name)
- List all the members of the "School of Applied Sciences, Technology and Education" department. (they explain: list all members means to list all the full name; full name refers to first_name, last_name)
- Among all the closed events, which event has the highest spend-to-budget ratio? (they explain: closed events refers to event_name where status = 'Closed'; highest spend-to budget ratio refers to MAX(DIVIDE(spent, amount)))
- What is the highest amount of budget spend for an event? (they explain: highest amount of budget spend refers to MAX(spent))
- What is the total amount of money spent for food? (they explain: total amount of money spent refers to SUM(spent); spent for food refers to category = 'Food')

## 4. Systems

The student club records live in the operational database (SQL Server). A copy is refreshed into the analytics warehouse copy (Snowflake) for reporting.
The team wants the automation to read from these systems directly, not to copy the data again.
